knowledge_point.title: Separating the Variables in a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Separate the variables in the following differential equation: 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={y}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡5x
$$

Work on a domain where all displayed expressions are defined.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A differential equation is *separable* if it can be written in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x)g(y).
$$

If an equation is separable, we say that the variables are *separated* when it is written in the form

$$
\frac{1}{g(y)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x).
$$

Notice that our differential equation is separable since it can be written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡5x\cdot {y}^{4}.
$$

Therefore, we separate the variables as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{{y}^{4}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡5x
$$

generation.domain: y≠0; raw distractors containing csc additionally require sin(5x)≠0

question.:question/problem:
Separate the variables in the following differential equation: 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x}{4x+2x{y}^{2}+4+2{y}^{2}}
$$

Work on a domain where all displayed expressions are defined.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A differential equation is *separable* if it can be written in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x)g(y).
$$

If an equation is separable, we say that the variables are *separated* when it is written in the form

$$
\frac{1}{g(y)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x).
$$

Notice that our differential equation is separable since it can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x}{(2x+2)(2+{y}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{x}{2x+2}\cdot \frac{1}{2+{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we separate the variables as follows:

$$
(2+{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x}{2x+2}
$$
